text.brief: In March 1942 Wang Shiwei published an essay called Wild Lilies in the Party's Liberation Daily that mocked the privileges of senior cadres at Yan'an.
text.record: Mao launched the Rectification Movement that spring, and Party meetings denounced Wang as a Trotskyite through May and June 1942 ([Independent Chinese PEN Center: Wang Shiwei (NGO, secondary)](https://www.chinesepen.org/english/no-13-yu-zhang-case-no-1)). The Party expelled Wang and held him under guard, and its security forces executed him in 1947 ([Independent Chinese PEN Center: Wang Shiwei (NGO, secondary)](https://www.chinesepen.org/english/no-13-yu-zhang-case-no-1)). The Ministry of Public Security concluded in 1991 that the Trotskyite charge had no basis ([Aisixiang essay by Fu Guoyong, "Pursuing humanity: rereading Wang Shiwei" (Chinese essay site, secondary)](https://www.aisixiang.com/data/415.html)).
text.reading: Rectification made one writer the example for every writer, which is Stratagem 26. The Party learned at Yan'an to manufacture coherence by study, confession and purge, and Robert Lifton later drew his criteria of totalism from people who went through the same method.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No body inside the Party could protect a member who told the truth about its privileges.
text.fix: Protect the internal critic by rule, because an organization that punishes accurate reports soon receives none.
